extracted.intended_audience: readers seeking recommendations and creative-writing students
extracted.subtask_description: An individual author's policy for writing Goodreads reviews intended to recommend books and teach writing students by highlighting what the author liked and the techniques worth studying. The reviews prioritize constructive, non-spoiler commentary and disclosure of any ties or biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Only post favorable reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Because of these goals, you will find only favorable reviews there. In fact, as I’m only posting on there books that I liked, I will rate everything at an even five-star level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page is curated only to list books the author enjoyed; negative opinions are not posted. This policy is intentional to avoid prominent authors appearing to 'gun for' others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use five-star ratings consistently; focus less on stars
rubrics_metrics.description: I will rate everything at an even five-star level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers should focus more on the review text than the star rating—star ratings are uniform and not diagnostic of nuanced opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary focus: what I liked, not plot summaries
rubrics_metrics.description: I’m not a professional reviewer, and my objective is not to tell you what the book is about. Instead, I’ll talk about what I liked in it...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews will avoid lengthy plot summaries; emphasis is on the aspects the reviewer found effective and instructive for writers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid spoilers
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoiding spoilers for the most part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews should generally keep plot reveals to a minimum so as not to spoil the reading experience for others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include a section on what the writer does well (teaching focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every review will have a section talking about what I think the writer does particularly well, and highlight things that I think writing students should study when reading the book, to learn techniques they might apply to their own fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly identify techniques, strengths, and instructive elements in the work so students can learn craft; use examples but avoid spoiling key plot beats.

rubrics_metrics.name: End with a short overview recommendation and reader-type guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: At the end of the review, I’ll give a shorter 'overview style' recommendation, explaining the types of readers I think will like the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise recommendation that helps potential readers determine fit (genres, reader preferences, tone, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Include brief content warning only if applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Included in this will be a brief content warning, if one applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only add content warnings when material exceeds the stated threshold (see next criterion). Keep warnings short and relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content warning threshold: only above mild PG-13
rubrics_metrics.description: For this, assume that I’m not going to mention anything that is below a mild PG-13 level rating. Common swear words, action-adventure style violence, and mild sensuality won't merit a mention here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not flag commonplace coarse language, routine adventure violence, or mild sensuality. Reserve warnings for content more severe than a mild PG-13 standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose ties or biases to the author
rubrics_metrics.description: I will mention any ties I have to the author, or biases I might have in suggesting the book, just to be clear and on the record about such things.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be transparent about personal connections, professional relationships, or other potential conflicts of interest that might affect the recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer silence over public negative criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: A famous author once said to me early in my career, 'Don’t worry. If your book works for me, I’ll talk about it. If it doesn’t, I just won’t say anything.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use the platform to publicly attack or harshly criticize other authors; if a work doesn't appeal, opt not to post rather than post negative commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain dual goals: reader recommendations + instructional examples
rubrics_metrics.description: I maintain the page for two reasons. First, to have a list of books I have enjoyed to which I can point readers who ask me for book recommendations. Second, to give some examples of different types of writing, and make some notes on them for writing students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure reviews so they serve both as useful reader recommendations and as pedagogical examples—balance personal taste with craft-focused observations.
